name: t_selection_mstca_v1
purpose: Reduce normal-condition false alarms of the MSTCA baseline (S0 / M0 architecture) by fixing the training-length and checkpoint-selection protocol. The S-group showed checkpoint/seed effects (20-80%) far larger than structural effects (<=10%), and inner-CE selection tends to pick early epochs (docs/research/2026-11-07/S组结构消融结果_阶段1_v1.md, _阶段2_v1.md).
baseline_architecture: mstca (S0) only. The model is fixed; this protocol changes only training length and checkpoint selection.

sections: data: root, population, outer_folds, inner_selection (same 's_ablation_inner_v1|' hash and expected sizes), never_read, identity_check
training: recipe, sampler, loss, optimizer, schedule, determinism, model_rng
evaluation.uncertainty (association_group cluster bootstrap, 2000 replicates, rng seed 20261106, one resample shared by all arms and seeds)
differences: no early stopping: every run trains all 100 epochs
a checkpoint is saved after every epoch
selection rules are applied after training, using only inner predictions or fixed epochs

initialization_goldens: Seeds 42-44 use the existing goldens in tests/test_mstca_ablation_factory.py. Goldens for (mstca, 45) and (mstca, 46) are generated once on the local CPU during implementation and pinned in tests/test_t_selection.py before any formal run; they must match on the server under ATEN_CPU_CAPABILITY=default. Never regenerate on the server.

trajectory.per_run: One run per (seed, fold): train 100 epochs with the inherited recipe. After each epoch e, in eval mode: save checkpoint_e; predict all inner windows and all outer held-out windows; store the fault probabilities per epoch.
trajectory.rng_isolation: Per-epoch inner and held-out inference must not consume any RNG used by training: every extra DataLoader has its own explicit torch.Generator, shuffle=False, num_workers=0. The reproduction gate detects violations.
trajectory.heldout_use: Per-epoch held-out predictions are used only (a) to read out the epoch that each pre-declared rule selected from inner or fixed information and (b) for the descriptive oracle curve. They never feed a selection rule.

T0.definition: Exactly the S-protocol selection, replayed post hoc: compute the inner class-balanced CE each epoch with the same computation as inner_ce() in scripts/research/train_s_ablation.py (float64, mean of the two per-class means); feed epochs 1..100 in order to the same selection_step() logic (initial state best_loss=inf, reference=inf, bad_epochs=0; best on strict improvement, so earliest on ties; reference reset on loss < reference*0.995; bad_epochs incremented only for epochs > 30; stop at the first epoch > 30 with bad_epochs >= 20). T0 = best_epoch at the stop epoch, or at epoch 100 if no stop occurs. Equals S0 for seeds 42-44.

T1.definition: Checkpoint of epoch 100 (end of the cosine schedule). Uses no inner information.

T2.definition: Epoch e in 1..100 minimising inner FP@R97 (inherited FP@R97 definition applied to the inner windows of that run); ties go to the later epoch.

T3.definition: Per window, arithmetic mean of the fault probabilities of the five T1 models (seeds 42-46) that did not train on its fold. Secondary; deployment cost 5x MACs.

gates_in_run.reproduction: For seeds 42, 43, 44 and every fold: (1) the state_digest of the T checkpoint at the S0 best_epoch must equal checkpoint_state_digests.best in artifacts/s_ablation_mstca_v1/cv/S0_seed<s>_fold<f>/report.json; (2) the T0 rule applied to the T run's inner-CE history must select the same epoch as S0. Any mismatch: STOP and report; do not continue the sequence.
gates_in_run.evaluation_reproduction: T0 pooled held-out FP@R97 for seeds 42, 43, 44 must equal the S0 values in artifacts/s_ablation_mstca_v1/evaluation_cv/evaluation.json (3595, 3588, 4610).

evaluation.population: Phase 1: pooled outer held-out predictions per (arm, seed) over all 162069 train windows.

secondary: T3 vs T1: ensemble FP@R97 divided by the geometric mean of the five T1 single-model FP@R97

evaluation.ratio: FP@R97(arm) / FP@R97(T0) per seed; seed aggregate = geometric mean over the 5 seeds. Same paired cluster bootstrap; t* recomputed per arm, seed and replicate.
secondary_metrics: AP; per-seed delta AP and its arithmetic seed mean with bootstrap CI
FP@R97 counting only normal windows outside late_hover_normal (t* unchanged)
late_hover_normal FP at t* and at p > 0.5, split SIL/HIL
per-class fault recall at t* outside late_hover_fault; GPS and barometer recall on late_hover_fault
across-seed SD of log FP@R97 per arm (seed stability)
evaluation.descriptive_only: Held-out FP@R97 versus epoch per seed (pooled over folds) and the oracle epoch minimising it, labelled NOT SELECTABLE; shown only as headroom.
evaluation.multiplicity: Two primary comparisons, no correction; both reported regardless of outcome.

decision_rules.precedence: Take the first that holds: INCONCLUSIVE by undefined_policy -> seed-inconsistent branch (see seed_consistency) -> TRADE_OFF (class constraint) -> BETTER (upper 95% bound < 1.0) -> WORSE (lower 95% bound > 1.0) -> EQUIVALENT (CI inside [1/1.10, 1.10]) -> INCONCLUSIVE.
decision_rules.seed_consistency: Seed-consistent means at least 4 of the 5 per-seed ratio point estimates strictly on the same side of 1.0 (exactly 1.0 counts for neither). A seed-inconsistent comparison is resolved inside its own branch, in this order: class constraint violated -> TRADE_OFF (reason class_constraint_seed_mixed); else CI inside [1/1.10, 1.10] -> EQUIVALENT (reason equivalent_seed_mixed); else INCONCLUSIVE (reason seed_consistency). The class constraint therefore applies to every EQUIVALENT verdict.
decision_rules.class_constraint: At t*, no fault class loses more than 1.0 pp recall versus T0 (seed mean) on fault windows outside late_hover_fault. Violated -> TRADE_OFF.
decision_rules.AP_consistency: BETTER is contradicted when the delta AP 95% upper bound < 0; WORSE when the lower bound > 0. Contradicted verdicts become INCONCLUSIVE (reason AP_consistency). EQUIVALENT and TRADE_OFF only report delta AP.
decision_rules.undefined_policy: Inherited from s_ablation_mstca_v1 r2: no pseudocounts, redraws or dropped replicates; an undefined ratio or CI makes the comparison INCONCLUSIVE.
decision_rules.T3: ENSEMBLE_HELPS if the T3/T1 ratio 95% upper bound < 1.0 and delta AP (T3 - T1) upper bound is not < 0; otherwise NO_CLEAR_GAIN. Always reported with its 5x MAC cost.
decision_rules.adoption: The rule adopted for later experiments follows mechanically from phase-1 verdicts: (1) both T1 and T2 BETTER -> T1, unless the T2/T1 ratio 95% upper bound < 1.0, then T2; (2) exactly one BETTER -> that one; (3) neither BETTER -> T1 if T1 is EQUIVALENT, otherwise keep T0. T1 is preferred on ties because a fixed length removes selection noise and needs no inner set. Ensemble use is a separate deployment decision and never changes the adopted rule.

runs.phase1_cv: 5 seeds x 3 folds = 15 runs; all arms derive from these 15 trajectories.
runs.order: for seed in [42, 43, 44, 45, 46]: for fold in [0, 1, 2]. Seeds 42-44 first, so the reproduction gate is passed before any new seed runs.
runs.phase2_val: Only after phase-1 verdicts and their SHA256 are recorded: 5 runs (one per seed), fit = all train windows minus inner (as in S phase 2), 100 epochs, checkpoint and inner predictions every epoch. Then predict the 34710 source val windows once with the T0-selected checkpoint and once with the adopted-rule checkpoint (a single pass if they coincide or T0 is adopted). If T1 is adopted, T3 uses the five epoch-100 val predictions. No per-epoch val predictions.
runs.phase2_confirmation: Adopted rule BETTER: CONFIRMED if the val geometric-mean ratio vs T0 < 1.0. Adopted rule EQUIVALENT: CONFIRMED if inside [1/1.10, 1.10]. Per-seed values reported. Val never changes the phase-1 verdicts or the adoption.
runs.rerun_policy: Inherited: only after an infrastructure failure, with identical configuration and the failure logged; never change seed or settings to replace a completed run.

environment.host: operator logs in with ssh autodl_UAV; server preflight records hostname and nvidia-smi output
environment.required: torch 2.5.1+cu124, numpy 2.1.3, CUDA available, CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8, ATEN_CPU_CAPABILITY=default; all asserted, never setdefault
environment.golden_policy: Golden digest mismatch: STOP and report. Never regenerate goldens and never change the CPU capability setting without architect approval.

code_identities.hash_rule: sha256 of the file bytes after replacing CRLF with LF (line-ending independent; avoids the S-group CRLF incident)
code_identities.new_scripts: scripts/research/train_t_selection.py, scripts/research/evaluate_t_selection.py, scripts/research/preflight_t_selection.py and tests/test_t_selection.py are written after this freeze; their normalized SHA256 go into a pre-run manifest and must not change during phase 1 or phase 2.

outputs: artifacts/t_selection_mstca_v1/<phase>/seed<seed>_fold<fold>/ containing report.json, factory_receipt.json, checkpoints/epoch_<e>.pt, inner_predictions.npz (epochs x windows), heldout_predictions.npz (epochs x windows; phase 1 only), selections.json. Phase 2 val predictions only for selected checkpoints. Fresh directories only, never overwrite.
forbidden: internal test or any Real data
source val in phase 1; per-epoch val predictions in phase 2
using held-out or val predictions in any selection rule
changing arms, rules, margin, seeds or adoption after any phase-1 result is seen
dropping or replacing a seed; reporting only favourable seeds
modifying frozen S-group files or artifacts
regenerating golden digests on the server
preflight_gates: tests/test_mstca_ablation_factory.py and tests/test_t_selection.py pass on the server, including the 12 existing goldens and the 2 new (mstca, 45/46) goldens
protocol .sha256 lock; normalized code identities; nine data identities; outer fold and inner sizes
GPU determinism: seed 42 fold 0, 2 epochs, twice from scratch with the T runner, identical state digests
local CPU smoke committed: 2 epochs, <= 2048 fit windows, selection file and per-epoch prediction arrays written
budget: Phase 1: 15 runs x ~15 min, about 4 GPU hours. Phase 2: 5 runs x ~17 min, about 1.5 GPU hours.

revisions.change: seed_consistency/precedence: a seed-inconsistent comparison is checked against the class constraint before it can be EQUIVALENT (r0 allowed equivalent_seed_mixed even with a >1 pp class recall drop, which could make T1 adoptable despite a recall cost, inconsistent with the seed-consistent path where TRADE_OFF precedes EQUIVALENT).
revisions.reason: Found in architect review of the local implementation; no formal result exists.
